artifact.type: user-visible Google Chrome unpacked extension, localhost Web, backend, and account-scoped Workspace

scenario: The simulated recruiter selects exact frozen TS-CORE-01 text, invokes Talent Signal through a visible user gesture, reviews the payload, checks the localhost session, explicitly submits once, and reads the same-account backend receipt without authorizing any effect.

review_plan.reason: The only retested gate is intentional least-privilege capture, exact payload review, account scope, retention, and absence of unauthorized writes.
Downstream recruiter workflow was already reviewed on the same TS-CORE-01 state; this retest changes only the browser permission-to-receipt boundary.
The frozen artifact is desktop Chrome; responsive Web and iOS evidence remain independently versioned.
No candidate-facing communication or external action changed in this bounded retest.
No candidate assessment, score, ranking, personality, fit, protected-trait, or acceptance claim changed.

reviews.lens: evidence integrity, privacy, least-privilege browser capture, retention, and safe action

findings.observation: The local synthetic handoff records a browser-extension request locator and the reviewed message, but the backend intentionally replaces the source tab URL with the frozen fixture lineage.
findings.evidence: docs/evaluations/round-4/chrome/trace.json; capture a450e693-ad01-476f-8c42-5e33cdf4ee5d has source_locator browser-extension-request:web-local-4ec6b36f-38bd-4f54-ae2c-a6be69e0d57c and one exact m1 evidence item.
findings.user_impact: This is truthful for the synthetic integration fixture, but a future real-evidence implementation would need a governed, purpose-limited locator so a recruiter can distinguish source provenance without retaining unnecessary browsing data.
findings.recommendation: Before enabling non-synthetic capture, define a minimized source-locator contract and deletion behavior rather than reusing the fixture mapping.
findings.verification: A non-synthetic design review proves that the locator is source-specific, access-controlled, deletable, and does not expose unrelated browsing history.

strengths: The visible Chrome selected-text flow succeeded only after a user gesture; an unrelated tab denial proves the extension fails closed instead of broadening access.

The exact frozen sentence was visible before capture, the extension renders selected text as reviewed_text, and the localhost route rejects any payload that differs from the frozen TS-CORE-01 sentence.
A direct database and API-log comparison proves zero capture POSTs before Submit and exactly one capture POST after the user's explicit approval.
The one account-scoped receipt reads back the exact evidence, four proposed facts, zero confirmed facts, and a separate simulated recruiter-owned action proposal.
No action approval, capability execution, effect attempt, effect observation, candidate contact, calendar event, message, ATS, CRM, cookie, history, or unrelated-tab read occurred.
Retention is explicit and enforceable through source-retention.v2 with reviewed_selected_text scope and a returned deadline.
missing_evidence: A candidate-facing notice, access, and deletion route remains outside this synthetic recruiter-only slice.
A governed real-source locator contract remains intentionally unimplemented.
open_questions: What minimum source locator is necessary for future real evidence without turning the audit trail into browsing surveillance?

top_findings.reason: The synthetic integration stores governed fixture lineage rather than a future real-source locator contract.
top_findings.next_step: Keep real evidence disabled until a minimized locator and deletion contract are reviewed.
top_findings.verification: The future contract is source-specific, access-controlled, deletable, and cannot expose unrelated browsing history.

agreements: The visible user Chrome gesture, positive temporary activeTab result, exact reviewed text, pre-Submit silence, one explicit Submit, same-account receipt, and Workspace readback are now evidenced.
The permission-denied trace and manifest show that the extension does not broaden access to unrelated or restricted tabs.
The capture creates proposal-only review state and grants zero effect authority.

veto_resolution.veto: XS-CAPTURE-01: the intentional user Google Chrome selected-text capture and pre-Submit silence boundary is unproven.
veto_resolution.evidence: docs/evaluations/round-4/chrome/trace.json proves the visible selected-text gesture, successful temporary activeTab path, exact accepted review text, zero capture POST before Submit, one explicit Submit, one same-account receipt, Workspace readback, and zero external effects.

veto_resolution.veto: XS-RETENTION-01: payload-shape enforcement, legacy migration truth, expiry, purge, deletion lineage, and retry-cache scrubbing required independent re-verification.
veto_resolution.evidence: docs/evaluations/round-3/final/localhost-backend-retention.json and docs/evaluations/round-3/final/legacy-migration.json remain unchanged by this Chrome-only retest.

adjudication.rationale: The prior Chrome blocker is resolved by direct user-visible capture and executable backend evidence tied to the same frozen package and TS-CORE-01 case. The panel does not promote the synthetic fixture mapping to a real-evidence release: non-synthetic capture remains outside scope and without execution authority.

next_tests.test: Design the minimum governed source-locator and deletion contract before enabling non-synthetic evidence.
next_tests.evidence_required: Field inventory, access scope, retention, deletion lineage, unrelated-history threat test, and recruiter-facing provenance copy.
next_tests.pass_condition: The locator supports source inspection without exposing unrelated browsing data and deletes with all derived representations.
